rules.rule_en: Simple Present Tense is used to express habitual actions and universal truths.
Simple Present tense is used to denote scheduled events, habitual actions, and universal truths.
Present Continuous tense is used to indicate actions happening at the moment of speaking.
Present Continuous Tense denotes an action happening at the moment of speaking.
Present Continuous Tense expresses actions currently in progress.
Present Perfect Tense indicates a completed action with present relevance, often translated using completed action markers in Tamil.
Present Perfect tense indicates an action completed in the recent past.
Present Perfect Continuous tense describes an action that started in the past and is still continuing in the present.
Present Perfect Continuous tense denotes an action that started in the past and is still continuing in the present.
Use Present Perfect Continuous tense to describe an action that started in the past and is still continuing in the present.
The simple past tense is used to describe actions that were completed in the past.
Simple Past tense uses verbs indicating completed actions in the past.
Past Continuous tense uses 'was/were' + verb-ing to denote ongoing actions in the past.
Past Continuous Tense (was/were + verb-ing) indicates an ongoing action in the past.
Past Continuous Tense describes an ongoing action in the past.
Past Perfect Tense describes an action that was completed before another past action occurred.
Use Past Perfect (Had + past participle) to describe an action completed before another past action.
Past Perfect tense is used for an action completed before another action in the past.
Past Perfect Continuous tense indicates an ongoing action that started and continued in the past.
Past Perfect Continuous tense describes an action that was ongoing in the past up until another point or event.
Past Perfect Continuous tense indicates an ongoing action that started and continued in the past.
Future tense in English is often used to denote planned, certain, intended, or expected actions.
The simple future tense ('will') is used in Tamil translation to express scheduled, planned, intended, or expected events.
Future Continuous tense describes an ongoing action at a specific time in the future, typically translated in Tamil using the format [Verb root] + [கொண்டிருப்பேன்/இருப்பார்].
Future Continuous tense is used to describe an ongoing action that will be happening at a specific time in the future.
Future Perfect tense expresses an action that will be completed before a specific point or time in the future.
Use 'Future Perfect Tense' (will have + past participle) for an action that will be completed before a specific point in the future.
Future Perfect Tense indicates an action that will be completed before a specific time in the future.
Future Perfect Continuous Tense describes an ongoing action in the future leading up to a specific point.
The Future Perfect Continuous tense describes an ongoing action in the future that leads up to a specific point in time.
Future Perfect Continuous Tense indicates an ongoing action in the future leading up to a specific point in time.
Future Perfect Continuous Tense describes an ongoing action in the future that leads up to a specific point in time.

examples.note_en: I am eating breakfast translates to நான் காலை உணவு சாப்பிடுகிறேன்.
The teacher is teaching English translates to ஆசிரியர் ஆங்கிலம் கற்பிக்கிறார்.
Focus on the mapping between English Present Perfect markers (has/have + past participle) and Tamil completed action verb suffixes.
Present Perfect uses 'has/have' + past participle, translated in Tamil using completed action suffixes like '-விட்டான்/விட்டாள்'.
Present Perfect Continuous uses 'has/have been' + verb+ing, translated in Tamil using '-கொண்டிருக்கிறான்/கொண்டிருக்கிறாள்'.
Examples illustrate Simple Past tense transformations.
Examples illustrate Past Continuous tense transformations.
He had finished his homework before dinner. (Past Perfect)
The train had left when we arrived at the station. (Past Perfect)
Past Perfect example: We had painted the room before the guests arrived.
Past Perfect Continuous example: She had been reading the book for two hours.
The structures typically follow 'had been' + [verb+ing] to denote continuous past actions.
My mother had been cleaning the house since morning.
She will visit her grandmother tomorrow.
Structure: Subject + will have been + verb-ing.
The sentence 'The students will have been preparing for the exam for a month by next Monday' demonstrates the usage of the future perfect continuous tense.

passages.title: Present Perfect Continuous Usage
passages.text_en: This section illustrates how to translate sentences indicating ongoing actions that began in the past into Tamil using the Present Perfect Continuous tense structure.

passages.title: Present Perfect Continuous Tense Practice
passages.text_en: This table demonstrates how to translate Present Perfect Continuous sentences from English to Tamil. It focuses on actions that began in the past and continue into the present moment.

passages.title: Tense Translation Tasks
passages.text_en: This section provides a comparative guide for translating Simple Past and Past Continuous tenses from English to Tamil. It breaks down specific verb forms to demonstrate how completion and continuity are expressed in both languages.

Will be using - (ongoing action in the future)
Will be celebrating - (ongoing action in the future)
Will be talking - (ongoing action in the future)
Will be waiting - (ongoing action in the future)
Will be explaining - (ongoing action in the future)
Will be cleaning - (ongoing action in the future)
Will be fixing - (ongoing action in the future)
Will be writing - (ongoing action in the future)
Will be listening - (ongoing action in the future)
He will have finished his homework by 8 PM.
translations.ta: அவன் இரவு 8 மணிக்குள்ளாக தனது வீட்டுப்பாடத்தை முடித்திருப்பான்.

translations.en: She will have left the office before you arrive.
translations.ta: அவள் நீங்கள் வருவதற்குள் அலுவலகத்தை விட்டுச் சென்றிருப்பாள்.

translations.en: They will have built the bridge by next year.
I will have completed my project by tomorrow.
We will have reached the station by 6 AM.
You will have learned the basics by then.
The train will have departed when we get there.
He will have written the letter before noon.
She will have cooked dinner by the time you come.
translations.ta: நீங்கள் வரும்போது அவள் இரவு உணவைச் சமைத்திருப்பாள்.

translations.en: They will have finished the exam by 4 PM.
I will have cleaned the room before the guests arrive.
translations.ta: விருந்தினர்கள் வரும் முன் அறையை சுத்தம் செய்திருப்பேன்.

translations.en: We will have solved all the problems by next week.
translations.ta: நாம் அடுத்த வாரத்திற்குள் எல்லா பிரச்சனைகளையும் தீர்த்திருப்போம்.

translations.en: You will have received the parcel by Friday.
He will have read the book before the meeting.
translations.ta: அவன் கூட்டம் ஆரம்பிக்கும் முன் புத்தகத்தைப் படித்திருப்பான்.

translations.en: She will have visited Paris by the end of this year.
translations.ta: இந்த வருட இறுதிக்குள் அவள் பாரிஸிற்குச் சென்றிருப்பாள்.

translations.en: They will have planted the trees by next month.
I will have saved enough money by December.
translations.ta: நான் டிசம்பர் மாதத்திற்குள் போதுமான பணத்தைச் சேமித்திருப்பேன்.

translations.en: We will have painted the house before Diwali.
translations.ta: நாம் தீபாவளிக்கு முன் வீட்டை வண்ணம் பூசியிருப்போம்.

translations.en: You will have learned to drive by next summer.
translations.ta: நீங்கள் அடுத்த கோடைக்காலத்துக்குள் ஓட்டக் கற்றுக் கொண்டிருப்பீர்கள்.

translations.en: He will have fixed the car by evening.
translations.ta: அவன் மாலை ஆகும் முன் காரை சரிசெய்திருப்பான்.

translations.en: She will have finished her studies by 2026.
She will have been studying for three hours by the time you arrive.
translations.ta: நீ வரும்போது அவள் மூன்று மணி நேரம் படித்து கொண்டிருப்பாள்.

translations.en: They will have been living in Chennai for ten years by 2030.
translations.ta: 2030 ஆம் ஆண்டுக்குள் அவர்கள் சென்னையில் பத்து வருடங்கள் வசித்து இருப்பார்கள்.

translations.en: I will have been waiting for you for an hour when the train arrives.
translations.ta: நான் ரயிலில் வரும்போது உனக்காக ஒரு மணி நேரம் காத்திருந்திருப்பேன்.

translations.en: We will have been working on this project for six months by July.
translations.ta: ஜூலைக்குள் நாங்கள் இந்த திட்டத்தில் ஆறு மாதங்கள் வேலை செய்து கொண்டிருப்போம்.

translations.en: He will have been driving for five hours by noon.
translations.ta: அவர் மதியத்திற்குள் ஐந்து மணி நேரம் வாகனம் ஓட்டியிருப்பார்.

translations.en: The children will have been playing for two hours by the time it gets dark.
translations.ta: இருள் ஆகும்போது குழந்தைகள் இரண்டு மணி நேரம் விளையாடிக்கொண்டிருப்பார்கள்.

translations.en: She will have been teaching here for twenty years by next June.
translations.ta: அடுத்த ஜூன் மாதத்திற்குள் அவள் இங்கு இருபது வருடங்களாக கற்பித்துக்கொண்டிருப்பாள்.

translations.en: By next week, I will have been learning Tamil for six months.
translations.ta: அடுத்த வாரத்திற்குள், நான் ஆறு மாதங்களாகத் தமிழ் கற்றுக்கொண்டிருப்பேன்.

translations.en: You will have been reading that book for a week by tomorrow.
translations.ta: நாளைக்குள் நீங்கள் அந்தப் புத்தகத்தை ஒரு வாரமாகப் படித்துக்கொண்டிருப்பீர்கள்.

translations.en: The workers will have been building the bridge for two years by December.
translations.ta: டிசம்பர் மாதத்திற்குள் தொழிலாளர்கள் இரண்டு வருடங்களாகப் பாலத்தைக் கட்டிக்கொண்டிருப்பார்கள்.

translations.en: He will have been exercising daily for a month by next Monday.
translations.ta: அடுத்த திங்கட்கிழமைக்குள் அவர் ஒரு மாதமாக தினமும் உடற்பயிற்சி செய்துகொண்டிருப்பார்.

translations.en: She will have been cooking
They will have been travelling
Will have been using
Will have been waiting
Will have been barking
Will have been saving
Will have been practising
Will have been repairing
The students will have been preparing for the exam for a month by next Monday.
translations.ta: அடுத்த திங்கட்கிழமைக்குள் மாணவர்கள் ஒரு மாதமாகத் தேர்வுக்காகத் தயாராகிக் கொண்டிருப்பார்கள்.

notes_en:
p86: This page provides a framework for understanding Simple Present Tense through translation, highlighting its usage for habitual actions and universal truths or facts with clear English-Tamil sentence examples.
p87: This page provides a translation guide for basic tenses, illustrating how English Simple Present and Present Continuous sentences correspond to Tamil grammar, specifically focusing on habitual actions, universal truths, scheduled events, and ongoing actions.
p88: This page provides a comprehensive table mapping English sentences in the Present Continuous tense to their Tamil equivalents, focusing on identifying actions happening in the present moment.
p89: This page provides a structural overview of English Present Continuous and Present Perfect tenses, mapping them to corresponding Tamil translations and highlighting the verb aspect of completed actions.
p90: This page provides a comparative study of English Present Perfect and Present Perfect Continuous tenses with corresponding Tamil translations, focusing on identifying completed actions versus ongoing actions.
p91: This page provides a grammatical comparison between English Present Perfect Continuous tense sentences and their equivalent Tamil translations, emphasizing actions that are still in progress.
p92: This page provides a clear breakdown of the Present Perfect Continuous tense, illustrating how to translate sentences indicating ongoing actions that started in the past into Tamil.
p93: This page provides a table of various English verbs in the past tense alongside their corresponding Tamil translations, illustrating how completed past actions are expressed in both languages.
p94: This page provides a structured comparison of English and Tamil sentence patterns focusing on Simple Past and Past Continuous tenses, helping candidates understand how past actions are translated based on their completed or ongoing nature.
p95: This page provides a clear breakdown of the Past Continuous Tense by contrasting English sentence structures with their Tamil counterparts to illustrate how ongoing actions in the past are translated.
p96: This page provides a grammatical breakdown of Past Continuous and Past Perfect tenses, specifically focusing on how these English verb structures translate into Tamil context. It emphasizes that Past Perfect involves actions completed before other past events.
p97: This page provides a table of sentences demonstrating the use of Past Perfect tense in English, highlighting actions that were completed prior to another past action, accompanied by their Tamil translations.
p98: This page provides a reference guide for translating Past Perfect and Past Perfect Continuous tenses from English to Tamil, using practical examples to illustrate how actions completed in the past or ongoing past actions are structured in both languages.
p99: This page provides a table of English sentences in Past Perfect Continuous tense alongside their Tamil translations, emphasizing the translation of ongoing actions in the past.
p100: This page provides a comparative study of Past Perfect Continuous and Future tense structures between English and Tamil, illustrating how specific verb forms correspond to ongoing past actions and various future events.
p101: This page provides a table mapping English sentences in the simple future tense to their Tamil equivalents, categorized by the nature of the action such as scheduled, planned, or intended events.
p102: This page provides a clear guide on the Future Continuous tense with practical sentence examples demonstrating how ongoing future actions are translated from English to Tamil.
p103: This page provides a grammatical framework for Future Continuous tense, showing how to translate English sentences describing future ongoing actions into Tamil equivalents using the auxiliary structure 'will be + verb-ing'.
p104: This page provides a comprehensive breakdown of the Future Perfect Tense. It illustrates how the English structure 'will have + past participle' translates to Tamil, highlighting the concept of completed actions relative to a future reference point.
p105: This page provides a comprehensive table illustrating the usage of the Future Perfect Tense. It demonstrates how to translate sentences involving actions expected to be finished by a specific future time, showing both English and Tamil sentence structures.
p106: This page provides a clear structural guide for translating Future Perfect and Future Perfect Continuous tenses. It distinguishes between actions completed by a specific point in the future versus ongoing actions leading up to that point.
p107: This page from Vetrii IAS study material focuses on the Future Perfect Continuous tense, illustrating how ongoing actions leading to a future deadline are constructed in both English and Tamil.
p108: This page provides a table detailing the usage and Tamil translation equivalents for the Future Perfect Continuous tense, specifically focusing on actions that will be ongoing up to a future reference point.
p109: This page provides an example of Future Perfect Continuous tense usage in English and its corresponding Tamil translation, emphasizing how to express ongoing actions leading up to a future milestone.
